title: Progressive latency SLA and tenant-priority fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD-style ticket to define tiered latency SLAs for interactive and background inference, the error budget model, and a playbook for progressive degradation and tenant-priority fallback routing during capacity pressure. Deliverables: SLA table, canary and abort gates, monitoring queries, incident runbook snippets, and implementation acceptance criteria for the Console and runtime teams.
scope: Define latency targets (p50/p95/p99), availability targets, error budget calculations, tenant priority rules, fallback model matrix, canary gate thresholds, and dashboards/alerts required. Produce acceptance criteria for API and Dedicated deployments. Create a rollout plan and a staged enforcement timeline.
out_of_scope: Billing changes, per-tenant legal SLA contracts, integration with external billing systems, deep model accuracy SLOs (only high-level fidelity thresholds included). Private deployment packaging and offline upgrades are not required for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: SLA table published in Confluence with explicit numeric targets for three workload classes (interactive, streaming, background) and owner assigned
Console shows per-route SLA status (green/amber/red) and links to the relevant dashboards within the UI
Runtime implements a tenant-priority routing policy that can be toggled via config and honors a 3-level priority (gold/silver/bronze)
Canary rollout enforcer in CI rejects model deploys if canary burn rate > 2.5x baseline for 10m window (configurable)
Automated alerting: PagerDuty trigger when 30m rolling p99 exceeds SLA by 15% for gold tenants or 25% for silver/bronze
Error budget math validated in staging: 30-day error budget window computed and exercised with synthetic load test
Runbook section with explicit mitigation steps published and linked in Console for on-call
Acceptance tests: load-profile-based contract tests (p50/p95/p99) run in CI with pass/fail thresholds and recorded results
rollout_gates: Canary traffic: 1% production traffic for 1h with p99 within 1.2x target for interactive workloads
Burn-rate probe: synthetic burst of 3x baseline for 15m preserved under fallback routing without violating gold tenant p99 target
Observability readiness: dashboards and alerts verified by SRE and PM before 10% traffic expansion
Adaptive throttle test: when error budget depletion > 50% within a 24h window, autoscaling policy and tenant-shunt must trigger as documented
Fallback variant availability: minimum two compatible model variants per route (primary and quantized fallback) available in same region
metrics: Interactive SLA (gold): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms, uptime >= 99.95% (30d)
Interactive SLA (silver): p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 450ms, uptime >= 99.9% (30d)
Background embedding SLA: bulk job latency median per request <= 2s, 95th <= 6s, weekly availability >= 99.5%
Error budget: rolling 30d window, allowed error budget = 1 - availability_target; burn rate computed as errors_per_minute / allowed_errors_per_minute
Canary criteria: canary p99 <= 1.1x target and burn rate <= 1.5x baseline over 10 minute windows
